issues.competing_evidence: Araujo-Betancor+05 Table 5 gives 14,200±900 K from a low-state HST/STIS WD atmosphere fit. Schwope+93 §3.4 derives 8,500–10,500 K from low-state optical residuals but reports an ≈18,000 K alternative from mixed-state IUE/optical flux ratio. Mukai & Charles+86 uses a ≈9,000 K optical blackbody component, later described by Araujo-Betancor+05 as somewhat arbitrary; Szkody+88 ≈20,000 K is secondary-reported and questioned because Lyα is absent.
issues.why_it_matters: The component temperature affects comparisons of WD thermal state and accretion history; values trace different wavelength ranges, epochs and model assumptions.
issues.needed_action: Confirm the public catalog should prefer the 14,200±900 K low-state photospheric HST fit and retain all other state/method-specific estimates as separate measurements; do not average them.

issues.competing_evidence: Schwope+93 defines q=M1/M2=2.69(+0.43/−0.34), assumes a ZAMS donor M2=0.13±0.02 M_sun, estimates M1=0.35(+0.11/−0.10) M_sun and later uses 0.5 M_sun as a model input. Shahbaz & Wood+96 defines q=M2/M1=0.10±0.05 and derives M2=0.07±0.08 M_sun with i=45±5 deg. The inherited 0.67±0.70 M_sun field is not a direct measurement in either paper.
issues.why_it_matters: Mass ratios use opposite conventions, and mass/model choices affect evolutionary comparisons and inferred WD properties.
issues.needed_action: Choose whether the compatibility table should leave a single WD mass unset while exposing both source-specific solutions and assumptions in the measurement ledger; do not promote the later 0.5 M_sun model input or unclear 0.67±0.70 value as measured.

issues.competing_evidence: Ramsay+94 reports a low-state ROSAT PSPC rate 0.0187±0.0039 ct/s and an absorbed-blackbody fit with physically implausible emitting fraction. Ridder+23 Table 3 lists 1–10 keV=1.5×10^−12 and 0.1–10 keV=1.8×10^−12 erg s^−1 cm^−2, with X-ray reference Ramsay+94. Ridder+23 §3.2 describes generic catalogue conversions, but Table 3 does not map the exact MR Ser detector row, count-rate/band inputs, NH or absorbed/unabsorbed convention.
issues.why_it_matters: Flux band and absorption conventions materially affect comparisons with other CVs and any later luminosity calculation.
issues.needed_action: Trace the MR Ser entry to its exact ROSAT/catalog measurement and reproduce the Table 3 conversion/model; until then label these values as Ridder+23 converted summary fluxes and keep them separate from the native count rate.
